**Things to know**
- **`null` behaves differently.** `resolveToken(null)` throws a `TypeError` ("Cannot read properties of null (reading 'token')"), not the intended `Error`, because the default `{}` only applies to `undefined`. So I didn't test `null`. It does still throw, so it doesn't break the "returns or throws" rule, but the error is accidental.
- **Cases I left out on purpose.** `resolveToken("")`, `resolveToken({})` and `resolveToken({ token: "" })` all throw the intended error. I kept to the no-argument case you asked for; any of these could be added as more assertions.
- **The match is exact.** The test checks the full message string, so any rewording of that message will fail it. That's deliberate, but a regex would be looser if you'd prefer.
- **Hook prompt.** A project hook said `src/auth/PRECEDENT.md` has no `## token.test.mjs` section. My change doesn't make a new decision, so I didn't add one.
